strengths: Addresses a timely and underexplored problem: post-training quantization specifically tailored to DiT-based Real-ISR, which differs from both U-Net SR quantization and generic text-to-image DiT quantization due to sensitivity to fine textures.

The three components (H-SVD, VaSMP, VaTMP) are each grounded in clear motivating analyses (PCA of principal components in Fig. 4, layer-wise weight variance heterogeneity in Fig. 5, temporal activation variance trends in Fig. 6) and simple rate-distortion derivations, giving the design choices a principled flavor rather than being purely heuristic.

Extensive empirical validation: four real-world benchmarks, both W4A6 and W4A4 settings, comparison against 9 competitive baselines spanning diffusion-specific, DiT-specific, and SR-specific quantization methods, plus PEFT-based quantization baselines.

Thorough ablations isolating the contribution of each component (Tables 2-4), plus additional analyses on artifact localization (ROI-PSNR, Edge MAE, Color MAE in Table 9), calibration-set robustness (Table 8), and backbone generalization to DreamClear (Table 7).

Practical efficiency numbers are reported (peak memory, end-to-end speedup, runtime breakdown), and the paper discusses implementation details (parallel branch execution, Triton kernel for the local SVD branch) that lend credibility to the claimed speedups.
The limitations section is candid, acknowledging remaining W4A4 artifacts and the lack of native arbitrary-precision kernel support, rather than overselling results.
weaknesses: The core techniques build heavily on established building blocks (Hadamard incoherence processing from QuaRot/RobuQ, low-rank branch idea from SVDQuant, rate-distortion-based bit allocation similar to HAWQ-style approaches); the primary novelty is the block-wise rank-1 local SVD component and its application-specific instantiation for spatio-temporal precision scheduling, which is a comparatively incremental extension.

Generalization evidence to a second backbone (DreamClear) is limited to a single table (Table 7) on one dataset (RealSR) without ablations of the individual modules on that backbone, leaving the claimed backbone-agnosticism only lightly supported.

Some baseline results appear extremely weak (e.g., QueST MUSIQ ~37-45 vs. FP ~65-72, PassionSR/Q-Diffusion producing near-random LIQE scores), raising a question about whether these baselines were adequately adapted/tuned for the DiT4SR backbone and SR task, which could inflate the apparent margin of improvement.

The W4A6 DreamClear result where quantized MUSIQ/MANIQA/ClipIQA notably exceed FP performance is explained only speculatively ("mild perceptual regularizer"), which is not rigorously verified and could instead reflect known unreliability of no-reference IQA metrics under distribution shift from quantization noise, undermining confidence in some reported gains.

The theoretical derivations for VaSMP/VaTMP rely on several simplifying assumptions (Gaussian per-token/per-channel statistics after Hadamard transform, shared uniform quantizer distortion model across heterogeneous layer types) that are not independently validated beyond qualitative variance plots, and the greedy discretization/DP procedures are heuristic approximations to the underlying combinatorial allocation problem without optimality guarantees.

Hardware/setup for latency profiling (RTX 4090) differs from the main calibration/evaluation hardware (RTX A6000) without justification, and no statistical variance (e.g., multiple seeds/crops) is reported for quantitative results, limiting reproducibility confidence.
Code and models are stated as "will be available" rather than released, so reproducibility cannot be currently verified by reviewers.
